quick_notes.title: Ideology Recap
quick_notes.detail: Periyar (1925 Self-Respect). Kudi Arasu. Vaikom (1924). UNESCO (1970).
quick_notes.explanation: The Self-Respect Movement was a social reform movement started by E.V. Ramasamy, known as Periyar, in the year 1925. This movement aimed to give dignity and equal rights to lower-caste people and women by opposing caste hierarchy and religious superstition. Periyar published a Tamil newspaper called Kudi Arasu, which means "Republic," to spread these ideas of rationalism and self-respect. In 1924, a major protest known as the Vaikom Satyagraha took place in Kerala, where Periyar and others demanded that lower-caste Hindus be allowed to use the roads around the Vaikom temple. In 1970, the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) recognized Periyar as a great thinker by declaring him one of the world's most notable socio-religious reformers.

quick_notes.title: Politics Recap
quick_notes.explanation: The Justice Party was a political group formed in 1916 in the Madras Presidency, which is the area that is now Tamil Nadu and parts of surrounding states. Its main goal was to fight for the rights of non-Brahmin communities against the dominance of Brahmins in government and education. The first Premier, or head of the government, of the Madras Presidency from the Justice Party was A. Subbarayulu Reddiar, who took office in 1920. In 1944, at a conference in Salem, the Justice Party was renamed and reorganized into the Dravidar Kazhagam, or DK, which means "Dravidian Organization" in Tamil, shifting its focus to a broader movement for Dravidian identity and self-respect.

quick_notes.title: Policy Recap
quick_notes.explanation: The 76th Amendment to the Indian Constitution, which was passed in 1994, allows the government to keep giving 69 percent of government jobs and college seats to people from certain backward groups. This is called a reservation, which means setting aside a fixed number of opportunities for specific communities. The rule for this reservation comes from a report made by the Sattanathan Commission in 1970, which studied how to help people who are socially and educationally backward in Tamil Nadu. Before this, the 1st Amendment in 1951 had already changed the Constitution to let the government make special laws for such groups, so that these laws could not be challenged in court for being unfair.

quick_notes.title: Development Recap
quick_notes.explanation: The Gross Enrollment Ratio, or GER, is a number that shows how many students are enrolled in a school or college compared to the total number of children who should be in that age group; for example, a GER of 51 percent means that for every 100 children of the right age, only 51 are actually in school. In Tamil Nadu, a leader named Kamaraj started the Mid-Day Meal Scheme, which gives a free cooked lunch to children in government schools to encourage them to attend and stay healthy. Later, another leader named MGR improved this by adding a Nutritious Meal Programme, which provided a more balanced meal with extra nutrients to fight malnutrition. In Namakkal district, a special Egg Scheme was introduced, where children in schools receive a free egg each day to add protein to their diet. Finally, Sivakasi is a town in Tamil Nadu known as the "Japan of India" because it has many small factories that produce fireworks, safety matches, and printing work, making it a major industrial hub.

quick_notes.title: e-Gov Recap
quick_notes.detail: TNeGA. Uzhavan App. Naan Mudhalvan. e-Sevai.
quick_notes.explanation: e-Governance means using computers and the internet to deliver government services to citizens. TNeGA stands for Tamil Nadu e-Governance Agency, which is the government body that creates and manages digital services for the state. The Uzhavan App is a mobile application for farmers to get information on weather, crop prices, and subsidies. Naan Mudhalvan is a Tamil Nadu government program that provides skill training and job opportunities to students and youth. e-Sevai is an online platform where citizens can apply for certificates like birth, death, and income certificates without visiting a government office.
